clue.text: Start on course without refreshment, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the phrase before it is to be spoken and matched by sound

blocks.note: with tea off the menu there is no refreshment

explanation.surface: A golfer begins a round without stopping for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea off' and the golfing phrase are said the same way; only the spelling of the first word changes.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, players begin each hole by striking the ball from the raised peg, so the phrase means to begin a round.

clue.text: Music makers produce sombre tone, mostly inharmonious

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word just before is dropped
letters out of harmony are jumbled, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the word tone without its final letter

explanation.surface: A band's instruments are making a gloomy, out-of-tune noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Trombones are brass instruments, and any instrument is something that makes music.

clue.text: Put in charge of part of field event, rustic style

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters are a stretch lying inside the words that follow

blocks.note: surface padding: the letters start in the next word
the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next
surface padding completing the picture of a country sports day

explanation.surface: Someone is handed responsibility for an item at a country sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in evENT RUSTic, ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone responsibility for a task or a thing is to place it in their care, which is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: His takings are illicit in the main

definitions.text: His takings are illicit in the main

blocks.clueFragment: His takings are illicit in the main
blocks.note: surface reading: a man who mostly earns his money dishonestly
setter's reading: the main is the open sea, where this robber seized his loot

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'for the most part', but the main is an old word for the sea, where a pirate plunders ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate or buccaneer who plunders vessels for booty takes his gains illegally on the high seas.

clue.text: Withdrew action when settlement admitted .

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a deed is an action
a camp is a temporary settlement

explanation.surface: Legal action was dropped once an agreement had been conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' wants to be a legal agreement that ends an action; here it is a place where people settle.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave suddenly, often secretly, is to pull out, so the past tense matches withdrew.

clue.text: Puts ginger in spirits to blend -- some cocktail!

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barman adds ginger to liquor to create a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger here is spirit or pluck, and spirits are a person's mood, not liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone courage or nerve is to lift their mood with fresh pluck, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Competent student in lincoln

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: Abe, short for Abraham, the first name of President Lincoln
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A capable pupil studying in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside ABE; Lincoln is read as Abraham Lincoln, not the English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the skill or capacity to do something well is to be capable and qualified.

clue.text: Ceremonial display, one that is uplifting in Italy

definitions.note: the definition is a description: a place found in Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue something lifted up is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

blocks.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
Roman numeral one
i.e., Latin id est

explanation.surface: A grand ceremony in Italy proves inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is the abbreviation i.e.; with the one before it, both are read bottom to top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town buried by Vesuvius lies near Naples, a site located in that country.

clue.text: Fine macaroni

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, first-rate
second meaning: an 18th-century fop who copied continental fashions

explanation.walkthrough: Macaroni is not pasta here: it was the name for a vain, overdressed young man in Georgian England, as in Yankee Doodle.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means splendid; as a noun it is a man obsessed with clothes, as a macaroni was.

clue.text: To move briskly .when climbing is wrong

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Hurrying is a mistake when going uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's pace between walking and cantering, or any person jogging along, is a quick steady gait.

clue.text: ) A tour we arranged to last longer

indicators.note: arranged means put into an order, here a new one

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: We organised a trip that went on longer than planned.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast something, especially in wear and use, is to survive beyond it in time.

clue.text: Huntsman twice repeating gospel

definitions.note: a description of the character: one who makes a thing gospel by saying it, then repeating it twice

blocks.note: first meaning: the leader of the hunt in Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark
second meaning: that same leader's rule, 'What I tell you three times is true'

explanation.walkthrough: In Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark the leader declares 'What I tell you three times is true': say it, then repeat it twice, and it is gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain of Carroll's nonsense expedition hunts the Snark and rings a bell, so he is a huntsman by role.

clue.text: Common law man in the flying squad?

blocks.note: first meaning: old slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform
second meaning: a large buzzing fly, a member of a squad that flies

explanation.walkthrough: Common here means slang, and the Flying Squad is a real London police unit, which makes the fly sound like a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is dated British slang for a constable and also the name of a metallic blue fly.

clue.text: Extremely light

blocks.note: first meaning: to a great degree
second meaning: a flare fired from a pistol

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests 'extremely light' as in weight, but the second sense is the signal flare.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word intensifies like exceedingly; a signalling flare shot from a pistol carries the same name.

clue.text: Just like Bill Brewer and companions

blocks.note: first meaning: impartial, fair in judgement
second meaning: the riders in the folk song Widecombe Fair, who had a mind to go to the fair

explanation.walkthrough: Bill Brewer, Jan Stewer and the rest borrow Tom Pearce's grey mare to ride to Widecombe Fair in the Devon folk song, so they were set on the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impartial and even-handed is being just, and the hyphenated word also jokingly means intent on going to a fair.

clue.text: Secure employment in broadcasting organisation

blocks.note: to net is to secure, as a catch or a profit
work is employment

explanation.surface: Landing a job at a TV or radio company.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of linked television or radio stations sharing programmes is the usual name for a broadcaster.

clue.text: Chief manufacturer in Warwick, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: one who makes a ruler
second meaning: the Earl of Warwick, who set up and deposed kings in the Wars of the Roses

explanation.walkthrough: Warwick looks like the English town with a factory; it is Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, nicknamed for his power over the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with power to install rulers or leaders, as Warwick did with Edward IV and Henry VI, earns this name.

clue.text: Time to make melody, taking off the record

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
to sing is to make melody

explanation.surface: It is time to make music, wiping the old recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the record' suggests secrecy; here it is literally wiping a tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiping data from a tape or document removes it, and the gerund matches the -ing of the definition.

clue.text: Large stand needed for gathering of stars

blocks.note: great means large
to bear is to stand, as in 'I can't stand it'

explanation.surface: A big stage is required for a meeting of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars means celebrities in the surface, but the gathering is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major, the constellation containing the Plough, is a named group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Noticed ambassador with bottle opener inside drinking establishment

indicators.note: inside places the pieces just before it within the first word
an opener is what starts something, so take the first letter

blocks.note: seen means noticed
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title
first letter of bottle

explanation.surface: A diplomat was spotted with a corkscrew in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle opener' looks like a corkscrew but means only the opening letter of bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlicensed bar or illicit drinking den, a term from Ireland and South Africa, is a place selling alcohol.

clue.text: Provided with means to wind up incurred debts

blocks.note: to wind up is to end
having incurred debts, one owed money

explanation.surface: Someone is given money to settle the debts they have run up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being endowed is having been given funds or a permanent income, so one is supplied with resources.

clue.text: Dickensian needing no notes after thus accepting credit

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside another
after places the earlier-named pieces behind the ones named later

blocks.note: so means thus
CR is the abbreviation for credit
O is zero, nothing
G and E are two musical notes

explanation.surface: A Dickens character who will not spend on extras once he has borrowed money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No notes' looks like 'no money', apt for a miser, but it is a zero followed by two notes of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer, the miser of A Christmas Carol, is a character created by Dickens.

clue.text: Bill enters Open to play without restraint

indicators.note: a thing that enters goes into another, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: overt means open, not hidden
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A golfer called Bill plays freely at the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: Open is capitalised to suggest the golf tournament, and Bill to look like a man's name; both are ordinary words here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamming it up on stage means exaggerating a role, performing with too little restraint.

clue.text: Highly placed idols of the theatre

definitions.text: Highly placed idols of the theatre

blocks.clueFragment: Highly placed idols of the theatre
blocks.note: surface reading: top stars of the stage
setter's reading: the highest gallery seats in a theatre, which share their name with deities

explanation.walkthrough: Idols suggests celebrated actors, but they are divine beings, and the cheapest seats up in the top gallery carry the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Deities worshipped as idols share their name with the top tier of a theatre, the cheap seats up near the ceiling.

clue.text: Maxim for a writer

blocks.note: surface reading: a wise saying suited to an author
setter's reading: Maxim is the first name of a Russian author, so the clue asks for his surname

explanation.walkthrough: Maxim looks like a proverb, but it is a forename: the Russian novelist and playwright of The Lower Depths, also spelt with a Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of Alexei Peshkov, Maxim, belonged to a Soviet novelist and playwright, so it names an author.

clue.text: I am going before top part of the building is let

indicators.note: going before places the first piece ahead of the next one

blocks.note: I'm, the contraction of I am
a pediment is the triangular gable topping a classical building's front

explanation.surface: I am in front of the building's upper storey, which is up for rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Let is not about renting: it is the old noun for a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance' and a let in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstruction or hindrance is the archaic meaning of the noun, surviving in legal phrasing and in tennis.

clue.text: Nobleman in real trouble

indicators.note: a word in trouble is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is in genuine difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking above a viscount and below a marquess holds a title of nobility.

clue.text: Vessel in support of airman seen in ditch

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so this piece follows the one it holds up

blocks.note: FO is Flying Officer, an RAF rank
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A boat assisting a pilot who has come down in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' suggests an aircraft ditching at sea; it is the definition. The word is a variant spelling of fosse, a moat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fosse or foss is a long trench or moat dug as a defence, which is a kind of trench.

clue.text: Kind of music absorbing pussy's companion is fitting for boat trip

definitions.note: read as a fitting for a boat trip

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: rock is a kind of music
Edward Lear's poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat

explanation.surface: Music that takes in a cat's friend is suitable for a cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: OWL goes inside RO...CK. The Owl and the Pussy-cat went to sea in a boat, which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: The U-shaped pivot on a gunwale holding an oar is a fitting on a rowing boat for an outing.

clue.text: Send out carpet with reverse backing included

indicators.note: reverse means turn backwards, so the next word is read from its end
something included is put inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to carpet or rate someone is to scold them
aid is backing or support

explanation.surface: Delivering a rug with its underlay fitted the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet is the verb, to reprimand, and rate is an old verb with the same meaning; backing is support, not underlay.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit heat, light or energy outwards in all directions from a centre is to give it out.

clue.text: Productive activity needing plant and flower experiment

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Indus
a try is an attempt or experiment

explanation.surface: A gardener's hobby involves growing things and trying out blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is a crossword favourite for a river, read as flow-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufacturing is economic work that depends on factories and machinery, the plant of the trade.

clue.text: He runs daily

blocks.note: surface reading: a man who goes jogging every day
setter's reading: a daily is a newspaper, and he is the person in charge of one

explanation.walkthrough: Runs suggests jogging and daily an adverb, but daily is the noun for a newspaper published every day.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper's content directs its staff and decides what goes to print.
